market.regime: Stock-led: most stocks are holding up while the index is not

doing: The rule holds 20 stocks bought on rank and keeps each until it falls past rank 35. Average rank today is 17: 15 hold, 3 drifting (26 to 35), 2 past 35.
13 of 20 open positions are above their buy price, average +43.9% since purchase.
Last 13 weeks: book +7.1% vs universe -2.5%, ahead in 8 of 13 weeks. Last 52 weeks: +42.5% vs +1.9%.
50 orders across the last 13 weekly reviews. Trades closed in the last 3 months: 25, 48% profitable, average +5.9% after costs.
market: Regime: stock-led: most stocks are holding up while the index is not.
Nifty 50 closed at 22,603 on 2026-10-07, 7.0% below its 200-day average and 14.2% under its 1-year high. 1 week -0.5%, 1 month -5.4%, this year -13.5%.
The average liquid stock did better than the index: 1 month -5.5%, 3 months -2.4%, this year +4.7%.
Breadth: 50% of liquid stocks trade above their 200-day average (a month ago 64%), 25% above their 50-day (a month ago 49%). 6% rose in the last session.
Volatility: the equal-weight universe is moving 18.7% annualised over 20 days, against a typical 14.8% this year.

In the replay, weeks that started with breadth under 40% (43 of them) saw the book return +0.80% a week, +0.28% against the universe. Other weeks: +0.72% and +0.34%. The rule has no market-timing switch; this is context for what to expect.
preds: Walk-forward test since 2021-07-16: each week's ranges were built only from earlier weeks. Of 5,440 one-week stock outcomes, 51.5% landed in the middle half (target 50%) and 81.0% in the 8-in-10 range (target 80%). The ranges are about right.
2026 so far: a held stock was expected to make +0.79% a week and made +0.84%. The whole book was expected to make +0.72% a week and made +0.78%, inside its middle-half range in 59% of weeks.
The ranges hold up, but the expected return itself ran too high in 2021, 2022, 2025 and too low in 2023. Read the middle line as an average across good and bad years, not a promise for this one.
Over the last 52 weeks the forecast path compounded to +45.1% and the book actually made +42.5%.
One stock's one-week move is mostly noise: the middle half runs from about -3% to +4%. The forecast is useful across the whole book and over months, not for any single name.
